title: Claude Code launch and Agent Connect
summary: Engine services that launch Claude Code (stream-JSON child and terminal tabs), track outside agent clients with per-client and per-tool allow/ask/deny policies, approvals, limits and an activity log, plus setup/agents.py that syncs and drift-checks the skills.
description: Three layers. `services/claude_code.py` finds the claude CLI, starts a stream-JSON child (`start`, `send`, `stop`, `answer`) or builds a terminal launch (`open_terminal`, using `services/terminal.py` from `ui.terminal-dock`). `services/agents.py` is Agent Connect: sessions, identity, policy table (default ask; risky tools `save_project`, `export_image`, `timeline_render`, `convert_file` ask before overwriting), `approval` waits up to 120 s, limits, a 200-entry activity log and a subscriber queue for the window. `routers/agents.py` and `routers/claude_code.py` expose them (REST plus WebSockets, loopback only). `setup/agents.py` is the pattern formslot should extend: `agents sync` mirrors skills into .agents/skills and regenerates reference files, `--check` fails on drift. The commands reference it regenerates reads the catalogue from `svc.command-catalogue`.

invariants.text: The engine is reached on loopback only, behind the app-wide LocalGuard middleware (app/core/local_guard.py, not in this corpus); routes that act (start processes, write settings or secrets, WebSockets) also check the request origin with require_local or origin_ok.
Tools in RISKY_TOOLS (those that overwrite a file) require approval unless the client policy is allow; the default policy is ask.
agents sync --check fails while the mirrored skills or generated references differ from their source; run agents sync after the tool or command catalogue changes.
Mutating routes and WebSockets check the request origin (require_local, origin_ok) before doing work.
